precepts.text: Moses said if ye will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord until his enemies be driven out, then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession.
precepts.point: The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.
precepts.why:
Joshua tells the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh, “Ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day, but have kept the charge of the commandment of the Lord your God.” The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: “If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord to war, And will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord, until he hath driven out his enemies from before him, And the land be subdued before the Lord: then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.”

Whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land. They did it, all of them armed over Jordan until the land was subdued, and so they are guiltless and the land beyond Jordan is theirs.

precepts.text: But if ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord, and be sure your sin will find you out.
precepts.point: The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.
precepts.why:
The condition had a warning on the other side of it: “But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.” Had the two and a half tribes stayed home while their brethren fought, that sin would have found them out.

They did not. Joshua's words, “Ye have kept all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you”, are the proof that they kept the charge and did not sin against the Lord in it.

precepts.text: Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, ate of the sacrifices of their gods and bowed down to them, and Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled.
precepts.point: Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.
precepts.why:
Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes to Gilead. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. It goes back to Baalpeor. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods. And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”

The men of Israel committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab, ate of the sacrifices of their gods, bowed down to them, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor. That is what the anger of the Most High was kindled over, and that is the history behind the man they sent.

precepts.text: The Lord told Moses to take all the heads of the people that were joined to Baalpeor and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that his fierce anger be turned away from Israel.
precepts.point: Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.
precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel. And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.”

The heads of the people joined to Baalpeor hanged up before the Lord against the sun: that is how the fierce anger of the Lord is turned away. This is the judgment Phinehas stood in, and why his coming to the two and a half tribes in Gilead meant business.

precepts.text: Phinehas rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, and thrust the man of Israel and the woman through, and the plague was stayed; those that died were twenty and four thousand.
precepts.point: Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.
precepts.why:
“And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.” One man of Israel was so bold he brought her to his brethren while the whole congregation wept. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit.

“And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand; And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel. And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.”

That is Phinehas. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead with the ten princes, everybody knew it was about to go down.

precepts.text: Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel.
precepts.point: They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.
precepts.why:
The children of Israel cite the proof from their own history: “Did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel?” “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.”

One man of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it. That is why they came to the two and a half tribes over an altar: if it was rebellion, it would not stay on the other side Jordan.

precepts.text: He that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath, because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord.
precepts.point: They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.
precepts.why:
“and that man perished not alone in his iniquity.” “And it shall be, that he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath: because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord, and because he hath wrought folly in Israel.”

Achan was burnt with fire, he and all that he had, for transgressing the covenant of the Lord. Wrath fell on the congregation, and the man did not perish alone. So the offer stands: if your land be unclean, come over and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God.

precepts.text: Whosoever will not hearken unto the words of the Lord, he will require it of him; the Lord requires it whenever you go off.
precepts.point: If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it.
precepts.why:
The two and a half tribes put their own lives on the line: “if it be in rebellion, or if in transgression against the Lord, (save us not this day,)”. If we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today. And if it was to turn from following the Lord or to offer burnt offering, meat offering or peace offerings on it, “let the Lord himself require it”.

Require it is the Lord's own word: “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.” The Lord requires it whenever you go off. So they call on the Lord God of gods, who knoweth, to require it of them himself if the altar was anything other than what they said.

precepts.text: Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen; only Israel could leave the pattern of the law behind as a witness.
precepts.point: Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification.
precepts.why:
The altar was “a witness between us, and you, and our generations after us”, so that if anyone ever said, “Ye have no part in the Lord”, the answer would stand built in stone: “Behold the pattern of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifices; but it is a witness between us and you.”

Why could that pattern stand as identification? “Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.” Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. The pattern of the law left behind is a witness that Israel was there.

The same thing is happening today with the northern kingdom. Our people left their own witnesses over here: the writings on the Los Lunas stone identify with the northern kingdom, and the traditions, artifacts, practices, laws, and books that are being brought out in the classes all prove our people were here long ago and that they are the children of Israel. Yet with all that proof out there, people still deny it, the very thing the two and a half tribes feared.

points: Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh and told them they had kept all that Moses commanded them and obeyed his voice; they had not left their brethren these many days, but kept the charge of the commandment of the Most High.

The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.

Now that the Most High had given rest to their brethren as he promised, there was no war going on, so Joshua sent them home: return ye unto your tents and unto the land of your possession which Moses gave you on the other side Jordan.
Rest did not end the duty; if their brethren ever needed them again they had to show up, as all the tribes did show up later in this same chapter.

The release came with a charge: take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.

Joshua blessed them and sent them away rich: return with much riches unto your tents, with very much cattle, with silver, gold, brass, iron, and very much raiment, and divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren.

The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
When the two and a half tribes came to the borders of Jordan they built a great altar by Jordan, an altar great to see to. They hid nothing; they built it on purpose so that it could be seen.

When the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation gathered themselves together at Shiloh to go up to war against them. They thought the two and a half tribes had built the altar to worship idols and do their own thing, and they were ready to cleanse it before judgment fell on the whole nation like it had before.

Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him.

Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.

One man of Israel was so bold he brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation while they wept before the door of the tabernacle. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit.

The delegation asked what trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to build you an altar that ye might rebel this day against the Lord. They saw the altar and immediately thought the two and a half tribes were going into idolatry.

Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us? All those thousands died in that plague, and Israel had just gotten into the land and gotten peace; why would anyone bring that thing back on the nation again?

Their reasoning was national: if ye rebel today against the Lord, tomorrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel. Judgment does not fall on pieces of the nation; Deuteronomy 28 happened to all of us, and they understood that, so they showed up quick, fast, and in a hurry rather than sit around and let it happen.

They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God.

They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.

The two and a half tribes answered: the LORD God of gods, the LORD God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion or in transgression against the Lord, save us not this day. They put their own lives on the line: if we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today.
If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it.

This is why they built it: for fear of this thing, that in time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the LORD God of Israel? The Lord hath made Jordan a border between us and you; ye have no part in the LORD.

They feared that generations later the children on one side of Jordan would tell the children on the other side that they were not the children of Israel, shutting them out from fearing the Lord, from the temple, the feast days, and the sacrifices.

The altar was not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice; it was a witness between us and you and our generations after us, a memorial, so the two and a half tribes could do the service of the Lord before him in the place he chose, along with the rest of the tribes, and nobody could stop them.

If anyone ever said to their generations, Ye have no part in the Lord, the answer would stand built in stone: behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between us and you.

Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification.

God forbid that we should rebel against the Lord to build an altar for burnt offerings, meat offerings, or sacrifices, beside the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle: the sacrifices belonged in front of the altar the Most High set in his chosen place.

When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord.

Now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD: because they were not going off, nobody had to die that day, and coming from Phinehas that meant everything, because if it had been rebellion he would have been the one to start it.

Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us.
The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt.
The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God.
